title: The Fake Signal
briefing_md:
Campus Nexus is the smart-building system of a university. It watches 2,400 sensors across the hostels.

At 3:12 AM on Thursday 16 October it raised a FIRE alarm for Hostel Block C, 3rd floor. The sirens woke 600 students, who stood outside in the cold for 40 minutes. The fire team found no smoke, no heat and no fire.

The wardens say sensor C3-SMK-114 has been faulty for weeks and want it replaced. The dean wants to know if that is really what happened — and whether it could happen again tomorrow night.

Your job: find out what really set off the alarm, and how to stop it happening again.
root_cause_options: Human error during an approved change
Bad or wrongly formatted input data
Test or staging activity hitting production
twist_md: The testing (QA) team has shared the record of their overnight automatic test run, and a message from their chat the next morning.

lines: 03:12:04  FIRE ALERT: smoke sensor C3-SMK-114 reads 812 (alarm level is 300). Hostel C, 3rd floor.
03:12:04  Rule used: ONE sensor is enough to raise the alarm (checking with a second sensor is switched off).
03:12:05  Sirens for Block C switched on.

rows: Student reports the sensor chirping at night

content.body_md:
The message the alarm system received at 03:12:03:

• Sensor: C3-SMK-114
• Smoke reading: 812
• Battery: 3.1 V
• Date and time written inside the message: 14 Aug 2026, 03:12:03
• Message number: 55120

lines: 03:11:59  New device connected from address 10.20.4.77, calling itself "nx-sim-02". No password was asked.
03:12:00  nx-sim-02 sent 1,204 sensor messages in 10 seconds.
03:12:10  NOTE: this live hub lets devices connect without a password.

messages.text: False alarm again?! Sensor 114 was chirping all last week, I raised a ticket.
Get that sensor replaced today. Students are furious.

content.prompt: Why did the fire alarm go off in Hostel C at 03:12?
content.output:
Most likely cause: the smoke sensor C3-SMK-114 is broken.
Reasons: open maintenance ticket MT-2290 (chirping), battery replaced 13 days ago, and it read 812 while no nearby sensor went up.
Recommended action: replace C3-SMK-114 and close the incident.

lines: 03:12:06  EVACUATE Block C, all floors (started by the one-sensor fire rule).
03:52  Sirens reset by the fire team with their key.

content.body_md:
Fire team arrived 03:19. Block C floors 1–4 checked with a heat camera. No smoke, no heat, no burning smell.
Sensor C3-SMK-114 tested on the spot with test spray: works normally, reads 4 in clean air.
All clear at 03:48.

content.subject: Night fire drill, Block C — report and recording
content.body_md:
The night drill in Block C started at 03:12 using a smoke machine near sensor C3-SMK-114.

All sensor messages from 03:00–03:30 were recorded (file: drill-2026-08-14) and shared with the QA team so they can reuse them in future tests.

The replay tool plays back recorded sensor messages. The QA team uses it to test the system.

Where it sends the messages: the setting BROKER_URL.
If BROKER_URL is empty, it sends them to the LIVE campus hub (left over from the first prototype).

Recording it plays: drill-2026-08-14
Speed: 100× faster than real time
Name it uses when connecting: nx-sim-02

evidence.title: QA team — automatic test run record

lines: 03:11:40  Nightly test run #1 started on computer ci-runner-02 (first run on the new testing system).
03:11:41  WARNING: setting BROKER_URL not found in the new system — left empty.
03:11:58  Step: play back the fire-drill recording.

messages.text: We moved the nightly test to the new testing system yesterday evening. Did anyone copy over the BROKER_URL setting? On the old system it pointed to the practice (staging) hub.
…no. And the tool falls back to the LIVE hub when it's empty. Oh no.

answer.root_cause_md: Before the twist, the maintenance tickets, the wardens' chat and the AI diagnosis all blame sensor C3-SMK-114. Careful teams notice the alarm message carries a 14 August date and an out-of-order message number (E03, E04), was sent by nx-sim-02 from the QA team's test computer (E05, E12), matches the recorded fire drill (E10), and that the replay tool sends to the live hub when its setting is empty (E11). The fire team found the sensor working (E09).
answer.post_twist_category: Test or staging activity hitting production
answer.post_twist_responsible: The QA team's nightly automatic test, moved to a new testing system, ran without its BROKER_URL setting, so the replay tool fell back to the LIVE campus hub and played back the 14 August fire-drill recording; the live hub accepted devices without a password and the fire rule needed only one sensor.
